Random number from a Uniform distribution

```{r}
#taking a random number - this distribution goes from 0 - 1
runif(1, min=0, max = 10)
#First value is how many random numbers you want
set.seed(5)
runif(5)
```

How for loops work
```{r}
set.seed(1)
r = NULL
for (i in 1:500) {
    #saving it into an r variable
    r[i]=runif(1)
}
r

hist(r, col = "green", breaks= seq(0,1,0.05))
```

Sampling
```{r}
#replace is like rolling a die --> bootstraping
set.seed(1)
sample(1:6,7, replace = TRUE)
```


```{r}
set.seed(1)
#a = how many numbers, b = mean and c = standard deviation
r = rnorm(10000, 0, 1)
hist(r, col="green", breaks=50) #breaking the data into 50 bins
```

Checking 
```{r}
sum(r<(-1.96) | r>1.96)/length(r)
#no we get proportion of values in the tails
```

Create a random dataset

```{r}
set.seed(1)
n = 4 #sample size
ng = 2 #number of groups
p = 1000 #number of variables 

r = rnorm(n*ng*p, mean = 4, sd =2)

#putting data into a matrix
data = matrix(r, p, n*ng)
data

#put names on columns
#paste when I want to paste some numbers in a vector
#sep for separator
colnames(data) = c(paste("HD", 1:4, sep=""), paste("D", 1:4, sep=""))
rownames(data) = c(paste("protein", 1:p, sep=""))
data
```

T test
```{r}
group=c(rep("H",n), rep("D", n))
group=factor(group, levels= c("H","D"))
t.test(data[1,]~group, var.equal=TRUE)
```

For loop
```{r}
set.seed(1)
pvals=NULL
for (i in 1:p){
    pvals[i]= t.test(data[i,]~group, var.equal=TRUE)$p.value
}

pvals
hist(pvals, col = "green", breaks= seq(0, 1, 0.05))
```

```{r}
set.seed(1)
data[1:100, 5:8] = data[1:100, 5:8] + 10 #gets skewed
pvals=NULL
for (i in 1:p){
    pvals[i]= t.test(data[i,]~group, var.equal=TRUE)$p.value
}

pvals
hist(pvals, col = "green", breaks= seq(0, 1, 0.05))
```

How to create a dataset with integers?
#Poisson distribution
```{r}
r = rpois(1000, 4) #mean is equal to 4

hist(r, col="green")
```

```{r}
r = rpois(1000, 25) #mean is equal to 4

hist(r, col="green")
```

Central limit theorem
--> sample size should be at least 30 or 50
```{r}
n_sim=10000
n=5
mu=NULL
for (i in 1:n_sim){
    rolls=sample(1:6, n, replace=TRUE)
    mu[i]=mean(rolls)
}
hist(mu, breaks=30)
```
Exponential distribution - can see what sample size you need to fullfill normal distribution
```{r}
n_sim=10000
n=50
mu=NULL
for (i in 1:n_sim){
    rolls=rexp(n,3)
    mu[i]=mean(rolls)
}
hist(mu, breaks=30)
```

Type 1 and type 2 errors
```{r}
n <- 4
SD <- 2
mu <- 10
n_sim <- 10000
pvals <- numeric(n_sim)   # preallocate instead of NULL
set.seed(2)

for (i in 1:n_sim) {
    r  <- rnorm(n, mu, SD)
    r2 <- rnorm(n, mu, SD)
    pvals[i] <- t.test(r, r2, var.equal = TRUE)$p.value
}
hist(pvals)
```

When the null hypothesis is accepted - you get equal distribution of p-values

```{r}
#we have 490 due to chance
sum(pvals<0.05)
```

Adjusting p-values
```{r}
p.adjust(pvals, method = "bonferroni")
sum(p<0.05)
```

```{r}
p.adjust(pvals, method = "BH")
sum(p<0.05)
```
